sample_unit: CT scans (cancer vs normal across internal, two external, and real-world test sets)
models_evaluated: deep learning colorectal cancer detection model (CT)

links.outcome: Radiologist detection accuracy with versus without DL assistance in intended use mode
links.effect: DL assistance improved radiologist accuracy: 93.4% vs 86.0% (internal test set) and 93.6% vs 85.3% (external test set 1), both p < 0.0001.
links.quote: In both the internal test set and external test set 1, the DL model yielded higher accuracy than that of radiologists (97.2% vs 86.0%, p < 0.0001; 94.9% vs 85.3%, p < 0.0001), and significantly improved the accuracy of radiologists (93.4% vs 86.0%, p < 0.0001; 93.6% vs 85.3%, p < 0.0001).

links.outcome: DL model performance compared with radiologists on the same test data
links.effect: DL accuracy exceeded radiologists in internal (97.2% vs 86.0%) and external set 1 (94.9% vs 85.3%), p<0.0001; in real-world set sensitivity was comparable (94.3% vs 96.2%).
links.quote: In the real-world test set, the DL model delivered sensitivity comparable to that of radiologists who had been informed about clinical indications for most cancer cases (94.3% vs 96.2%, p > 0.99), and it detected 2 cases that had been missed by radiologists.

links.outcome: DL model AUC on internal, external multisite, and real-world test sets
links.effect: AUCs ranged between 0.957 and 0.994 across the four test sets, including two external sets and a real-world set.
links.quote: In the four test sets, the DL model had the area under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUCs) ranging between 0.957 and 0.994.

screen.reason: Evaluated whether a deep learning computer-aided detection model improved radiologists' detection performance compared to unassisted reading across retrospective test sets.
